title: Adaptive layering and legend virtualization for high-series density
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Our time-series canvas becomes unreadable and slow when dashboards contain dozens to hundreds of series. Legends are long, keyboard navigation is noisy, and screen-reader users get overwhelmed. This ticket proposes a design and interaction spec for: 1) an adaptive rendering pipeline that composes series into density layers and defers low-importance draws, 2) a virtualized legend component that groups/aggregates series with progressive disclosure, and 3) accessible summaries and scrubbing announcements so assistive tech receives concise, meaningful feedback.
goals: Reduce average frame draw time for large-series charts (>=50 series) by ~40%
Introduce a legend virtualization pattern that keeps DOM size constant regardless of series count
Provide keyboard-first controls to group/unfold series and an ARIA summary mode for screen readers
Align color and spacing with design tokens so charts respect theme changes and high-contrast modes
acceptance_criteria: Render pipeline: series are bucketed into three density layers (primary, secondary, background) and low-priority layers are drawn at lower fidelity without visual regressions on typical dashboards
Legend: virtualized list supports grouping, search, and an explicit ‘focus group’ affordance; DOM nodes remain bounded (<100 nodes) even with 500 series
Keyboard: tab/arrow navigation cycles through logical groups, Enter toggles group expand, Space toggles visibility; focus state meets 3:1 contrast against theme tokens
A11y: ARIA live region announces an aggregated summary when scrubbing (e.g., “6 series in view: avg 12.4ms, top series X +2.1”), and a separate announcement for group expand/collapse
Fallback: SVG/canvas fallback preserves interactivity and accessibility for older browsers and for printed exports
Design tokens: chart spacing, legend padding, and series stroke widths are mapped to existing tokens (space.chart-*, token.color-series-*) and documented in the tokens registry
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha K.: Initial discovery complete. Benchmarked slow dashboards using the telemetry dashboard; 95th percentile frame time = 280ms with 120 series. Identified two primary bottlenecks: full-layer redraws and large legend DOM churn.

2026-02-25 - Marco S.: Prototype of density layering in branch refs/feature/density-render shows a ~35% improvement in synthetic scenes. Needs integration with KV cache and render scheduler. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/1492

2026-02-28 - Priya M. (A11y): Reviewed ARIA approach. Prefer aggregated announcements over per-series announcements; suggested adding an opt-in verbose mode for power users. Also requested keyboard labeling for group toggles.

2026-03-03 - Design review: Iterated legend UI to surface ‘Aggregate’ pill and a compact thumbnail for color-encoded groups. Approved visual direction; asked engineering to provide a perf safety toggle in the component API.

2026-03-05 - Marco S.: Added unit tests for virtualized legend list and keyboard navigation. Bottleneck remains canvas compositing on Safari — filing a follow-up ENG ticket for WebKit-specific optimizations.
decisions: Use a three-tier density model (primary/secondary/background) rather than dynamic per-series LOD to simplify cache invalidation
Expose an API prop `preferredRenderMode` (e.g., 'quality'|'balanced'|'performance') that maps to token-driven stroke widths and drawing fidelity
Legend virtualization will prefer grouping by source tag if present, otherwise by color palette proximity
tradeoffs_and_risks: Grouping may hide important outliers if aggregation heuristics are too aggressive — mitigation: add an ‘expand to outliers’ affordance and confidence indicators
Heavier client-side logic increases bundle size. Mitigation: split legend virtualization into a lazy-loaded module and use tree-shaking-friendly utilities
ARIA summaries reduce granularity for screen-reader users; mitigation: provide a verbosity toggle in component props
